content: Miconazole is an antifungal medication that is prescribed to treat various fungal infections, including athlete's foot, jock itch, and vaginal yeast infections. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor. Miconazole is available in several forms, including creams, lotions, powders, spray liquids, and spray powders for application to the skin. For vaginal infections, it is available as creams and suppositories. For athlete's foot, it is typically applied once or twice daily for one month. For other skin infections, it is used for two weeks. Vaginal infections are treated with miconazole once daily at bedtime for either three days (Monistat-3) or seven days (Monistat-7). Always follow the instructions on the package or your prescription label carefully. Do not use more or less of the medication or apply it more frequently than directed by your doctor. When using miconazole for skin infections, clean and dry the affected area thoroughly before applying the medication. Apply the cream or lotion sparingly and rub it gently into the skin. Wash your hands immediately after application to prevent spreading the infection. For vaginal infections, follow the instructions provided with the cream or suppositories. To use the vaginal cream, fill the applicator to the indicated level or place a suppository on the applicator as directed. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart, then gently insert the applicator into the vagina and push the plunger to release the medication. Remove the applicator and discard it if it is disposable. If it is reusable, clean it with soap and warm water after each use. Wash your hands immediately after application. Apply the vaginal dose at bedtime, as it works best when you remain lying down after application. You may use a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using the medication even if you get your period during treatment. Before using miconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to miconazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are taking. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using miconazole, contact your doctor. If you are using a diaphragm or condom for birth control and are being treated for a vaginal infection, be aware that miconazole vaginal cream and suppositories can weaken latex, so you should use an alternative method of contraception. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Miconazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience increased burning, itching, or irritation of the skin or vagina, stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store miconazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Miconazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. If you purchased miconazole without a prescription and your symptoms do not improve within four weeks (or two weeks for jock itch), stop using it and consult a doctor or pharmacist. If this is your first time experiencing vaginal itching or discomfort, consult a doctor before using miconazole. If you have previously been diagnosed with a yeast infection and are experiencing the same symptoms, use the vaginal cream or suppositories as directed. Do not share your medication with others. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor. Some brand names for miconazole include Desenex® Athlete's Foot Shake Powder, Desenex® Athlete's Foot Spray Powder, Femizol-M®, Lotrimin® AF Athlete's Foot Spray Powder, Micatin® Athlete's Foot Cream, Monistat® 3, Monistat® 7, and Zeasorb®-AF, among others.
